National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Kundan Singh & Another on 27 August, 2018

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                 REVISION PETITION NO. 18 / 2018

National Insurance Company Limited
through Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Limited
Kohli Market, Haridwar Road, Rishikesh through its
Authorised Signatory, Regional Office situated at
Jai Plaza, 56, Rajpur Road, Dehradun
                                                     ...... Revisionist

                                Versus

1.    Sh. Kundan Singh S/o late Sh. Kishan Singh
      R/o Village and Post Bhyundar (Pulna)
      Patwarivrit Pandukeshwar, Tehsil Joshimath
      District Chamoli

2.    Uttarakhand Gramin Bank
      through Branch Manager
      Branch Joshimath, District Chamoli
                                                   ...... Opposite Parties

Sh. Deepak Ahluwalia, Learned Counsel for the Revisionist

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.S. Verma, President
       Mrs. Veena Sharma,              Member

Dated: 27/08/2018

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice B.S. Verma, President):

This revision petition under Section 17(1)(b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is directed against the order dated 11.07.2018 passed by the District Forum, Chamoli in consumer complaint No. 06 of 2017. By the order impugned, the District Forum has allowed the application moved by opposite party No. 1 - complainant under Section 24A of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 for condonation of delay in filing the consumer complaint and has condoned the delay in filing the consumer complaint and admitted the consumer complaint for decision on merit.
2

2. The opposite party No. 1 - complainant filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum, Chamoli, alleging deficiency in service, on account of repudiation of the claim by the insurance company. Since the consumer complaint was not preferred within the prescribed period of two years' from the date of accrual of cause of action and hence an application under Section 24A of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 was moved for condonation of delay in filing the consumer complaint. In the application, it was stated that the complainant runs the business of wool knitting at Ghangaria, which got damaged in the natural calamity, which occurred on 16/17.06.2013. There are dues of certain persons upon the complainant, on account of which, he remained busy in his business activities at Ghangaria since June, 2017. There is delay of 62 days' in filing the consumer complaint, which is not deliberate. The complainant could not file the consumer complaint within time due to his bad financial condition.

3. The insurance company filed objections against the delay condonation application, stating therein that no sufficient cause has been shown by the complainant for condonation of delay in filing the consumer complaint and that the application is liable to be rejected.

4. The District Forum vide impugned order dated 11.07.2018 allowed the application and condoned the delay in filing the consumer complaint. Aggrieved, the insurance company has preferred this revision petition before this Commission.

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the revisionist at the admission stage itself and gone through the record.

6. In the natural calamity, the complainant has lost his business, on account whereof, he could barely maintain his family and thus, one 3 can imagine the plight which the complainant had undergone. The complainant has also stated that he was under financial constrain and once his business activity got retrieved and he was able to have some earning, he filed the consumer complaint. There was 62 days' delay in filing the consumer complaint, which in our view, was sufficiently explained by the complainant and the District Forum was justified in condoning the delay in filing the consumer complaint. The Hon'le Apex Court in its decision dated 10.11.2014 given in Civil Appeal Nos. 10120-10121 of 2014; Jeevanti Devi Vs. Commercial Motors and another, has held that the delay of 135 days' in filing the revision petition should have been condoned by the Hon'ble National Commission and the controversy should have been addressed on merits.

7. Learned counsel for the revisionist cited a decision dated 13.08.2018 of the Hon'ble National Commission given in First Appeal No. 451 of 2014; New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Girdhar Kumar Saraf, wherein it was held that in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State Bank of India Vs. M/s B.S. Agricultural Industries (I); 2009 AIR SCW 2911, the Consumer Forum is duty bound to ensure that either the consumer complaint has been filed within a period of two years from the date of cause of action or it condones the delay after proper appreciation of the reasons submitted by the complainant for such delay. There can be no dispute about the above preposition of law. In the present case, the complainant has shown sufficient reasons for not filing the consumer complaint within time. Learned counsel also cited another decision of the Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Piyush Goel, Virendra Arya and another Vs. DLF Home Developers Ltd. and another; II (2018) CPJ 38 (NC). In the said case, the possession of the properties was delivered on 11.10.2013 and 15.10.2013 respectively and the sale deeds were executed during 4 2015. It was held that the complainants were not able to bring out as to what prevented them from filing consumer complaint within period of two years of accrual of cause of action. In the present case, the complainant has moved an application for condonation of delay in filing the consumer complaint, wherein the reasons were shown for not filing the consumer complaint within time, which were found to be sufficient. Learned counsel also cited a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Perumon Bhagvathy Devaswom, Perinadu Village Vs. Bhargavi Amma (Dead) by LRs. and others; 2008 (4) Civil Court Cases 503 (S.C.), wherein it was held that the decisive factor in condonation of delay is not the length of delay but sufficiency of a satisfactory explanation. Learned counsel further pressed into service one more decision of the Hon'ble National Commission in the case of Ketan Consultants Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Suresh Dattaraya Namjoshi; III (2012) CPJ 60 (NC), wherein it was held that the person who seeks exercise of judicial discretion of Court or Tribunal in his favour in the matter of condonation of delay, must explain to the satisfaction of Court / Tribunal / Forum that he had "sufficient cause" which prevented him from filing the proceedings within prescribed period of limitation. As is stated above, the complainant has satisfactorily explained the delay in filing the consumer complaint and the District Forum was perfectly justified in allowing the delay condonation application, thereby condoning the delay in filing the consumer complaint. The revision petition lacks merit and is liable to be dismissed.

8. Revision Petition is dismissed at the threshold. No order as to costs. 

         (MRS. VEENA SHARMA)                (JUSTICE B.S. VERMA)
K
